canvas-01-2.description: Lower right part of Helmetta sheet 1 (October 1923), at 50 feet to an inch behind a heavy line: the strip south of John (today John Place) between the brook and Main. A row of eight tenements, house numbers 103 to 110, faces John near John Street, with sheds behind, and dwellings stand in the long lots of block 6 between the brook and Railroad Avenue. Railroad Avenue and the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division run down the middle of the part, with the freight house beside the track at John. East of the track, Main runs south-west with a few dwellings, sheds and a concrete block store in blocks 5 and 6A. The brook along the west side runs beside the heavy line that separates this part from part 1 of the sheet, and the sheet's scale bar is drawn at the bottom. Water pipes are drawn along John.
notes: John is today John Place.
Placed from one detected junction (John Place / Railroad Avenue) with the scale of sheet 3 and rotation from its measured lines; John Place / John Street lies just off the part. Low confidence.

Printed sheet 1 of Helmetta (Oct 1923; canvas labelled Index). Title cartouche, key, index, water and fire notes and a key map (1000 ft to an inch) in the upper right are not map. Two map parts at 50 ft, drawn at different angles behind heavy lines: part 1 on the left, Main Street and Railroad Avenue with the P.R.R. Amboy Division south-west to Saw Mill Brook (house numbers 601-644), no cross street; part 2 lower right, John (now John Place) east of the brook with tenements 103-110, Railroad Avenue, the freight house and Main Street (645-655).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: left part: Main Street and Railroad Avenue (P.R.R. Amboy Division) south-west to Saw Mill Brook, house numbers 601-644 (no street junction or rail crossing; a fit of the drawn Main Street and track centrelines to the modern lines (scale 7.9 px/ft) puts it on Main Street between about 40.3719 and 40.3689 N (RMS 3.1 m, track 4.5-6.3 m) but the position along the street is weakly fixed and drawn lot lines do not match modern parcel corners consistently; needs an independent point (the Saw Mill Brook culvert on Main Street, or a surviving lot corner identified on the ground), then an anchored part with px_per_ft 7.9 and north_deg about +15).

sheet-2-1.description: The American Snuff Co. works (Manufacturers of Railroad Mills Snuff) in Helmetta, Middlesex County, at 50 feet to an inch (October 1923). The mill buildings, most of them brick and sprinklered, run down the east side of the plant beside the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division: manufacturing, packing and shipping, roasters, tin can and paraffining rooms, an enclosed passage, the engine and water wheel house on the head race, and storage for bottles, wrapping material and snuff flour. West of the tracks stand the storehouses for snuff and empty packages, a box factory and wood working shop, a machine and carpenter shop and the large leaf tobacco storehouses on Brookside Place at the bottom. The head race and a brook cross the plant from the west, with wooden bridges and a drive. Maple crosses the upper half from Main to the west edge, with a lumber store house and dwellings along it; Erickson Avenue curves north from Maple to a club house and bowling alley at the top left. John comes up from Brookside Place on the west, and Railroad Avenue and Main Street run along the east side, where Main has a hose house, the company's general store and post office and a few dwellings. A note block on the fire protection and water supply of the works fills the bottom left corner and is masked out. Water pipes, hydrants, a 50,000 gallon water tank and the stand pipe are drawn.
notes: Erickson Avenue on this sheet is today the south leg of Club Drive (named after the club house it led to); modern Ericson Avenue meets Maple further north, off the sheet.
John is not drawn north of the head race; the modern John Street / Maple Street junction lies in the mill yard and is not used.
Main Street / Maple Street and the railroad crossing of Maple are excluded: Maple is not drawn through to Main.
Fitted rotation about 11 degrees from sheet 3, as on the 1910 edition.

sheet-3-1.description: Central Helmetta, Middlesex County, at 50 feet to an inch (October 1923), from Brookside Place in the north to John (today John Place) in the south. John runs down the west side of the sheet with the brook beyond it; Railroad Avenue, the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division and Main run parallel down the east side, and Willow crosses between John and Railroad Avenue near the middle. The blocks between John and Railroad Avenue (blocks 4 and 31) are lined with nearly identical two-storey frame company dwellings of the American Snuff Co., numbered along both streets, with small sheds and privies behind. West of John at the top stand the long American Snuff Co. storehouses for leaf tobacco in hogsheads and a storage building, with a note to see sheet 2 for their report; smaller dwellings line the strip between John and the brook further south. On Brookside Place stand the Avon Inn boarding house and the edge of the mill buildings of sheet 2. The passenger station and its platform lie beside the track, and St. George's Roman Catholic Church stands east of Main near the bottom. East of Main a few dwellings face the street, and Manalapan Creek with a backwater fills the upper right of the sheet. A part of the lower right corner, behind a heavy line, is an inset of Erickson Avenue (part 2). Five-inch and eight-inch water pipes and hydrants are drawn in the streets.
notes: John along the south edge is today John Place; John down the west side is John Street; Willow is Willow Street east to Railroad Avenue.
Main Street / Willow Street and one of two Railroad Avenue / Willow Street nodes are excluded (the modern Willow east of Railroad Avenue is not drawn).

Map, 50 ft, Oct 1923. Part 1: Brookside Pl south to John (today John Place) between the brook, John St, Railroad Av and Main St, with Willow; American Snuff Co. storage houses, Avon Inn, passenger station, St. George's R.C. church. Part 2: inset in the lower right behind a heavy line, Erickson Av (block 17, houses 5-10, moving pictures and storage), continued on sheet 2 across a dash-dot match line A-B.

sheet-3-2.description: Inset in the lower right corner of Helmetta sheet 3 (October 1923), at 50 feet to an inch behind a heavy line. It shows Erickson Avenue, a 30 ft street with the dwellings of block 17 (house numbers 5 to 10) along its west side and a single dwelling and outbuildings in block 1 to the east. At its south end the street turns into a 25 ft street running south-east, which crosses a dash-dot match line lettered A and B and continues on sheet 2 as the curving part of Erickson Avenue that leads down to Maple. A storage building and a moving picture house stand at the inner corner of the inset. The margin of the inset is marked no exposures, and the inset lies north of the American Snuff Co. mill, near Helmetta Pond, although it is drawn on the sheet beside Main Street and St. George's church. The street is drawn turned about 17 degrees from the main map of the sheet.
notes: Erickson Avenue here is today Ericson Avenue and the east leg of Club Drive; the 25 ft street crossing the match line is Club Drive.
Placed from the two edges of the street where it crosses match line A-B, carried from sheet 2, with the configured scale and rotation; low confidence.

sheet-21.description: Western half of the Noreg housing development in Center Township, Camden County, drawn at 100 feet to an inch on sheet 21 of the Gloucester City series (January 1923). The built blocks lie in the upper half of the sheet between Little Timber Creek and the marsh on the west and Chestnut and New Broadway on the east. Pershing Road curves along the creek side; Paris Avenue runs diagonally south-east from Pershing Road to Marne Road; New Jersey Road crosses the top of the blocks and returns down the west side; Pennsylvania Road and Marne Road run south-east through the middle; Chestnut runs north and south along the east side to the oval Town Center. The blocks are filled with small frame dwellings and brick or concrete row houses of the wartime shipyard housing, nearly all the same few plans, with house numbers along every frontage. A sewage disposal plant with a concrete tank stands at the edge of the marsh, a wooden foot bridge crosses Little Timber Creek to the north-west, and an island lies in the creek at the top. The lower half of the sheet is laid out but empty: the blocks numbered 300 to 317 south of Center between the continuation of New Jersey Road, Pennsylvania Road, a proposed street, Marne Road and Chestnut carry no buildings. Big Timber Creek runs along the west edge. The letters of Brooklawn are spread across the development. Water pipes are drawn in most streets.
notes: Center Township was incorporated as the Borough of Brooklawn in 1924; the 1930 edition of these sheets is atlas brooklawn-1930.
Center is today Center Street; Chestnut is Chestnut Street; the lower half of the sheet was laid out as planned streets in 1923.
Paris Avenue / Pennsylvania Road was detected 13 m off the fit and left out.

Gloucester City series sheet 21, Center Township (Camden County; today the Borough of Brooklawn), Jan 1923, 100 ft to an inch. Western Noreg village: Pershing Rd, New Jersey Rd, Paris Av, Pennsylvania Rd, Marne Rd, Chestnut, Town Center; south half planned streets; Big and Little Timber Creek. One part.

sheet-22.description: Eastern half of the Noreg housing development in Center Township, Camden County, at 100 feet to an inch on sheet 22 of the Gloucester City series (January 1923). The top of the sheet is a platted grid between Lake Drive and Browning Lane: Railroad Avenue, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th Streets crossed by Centre, with numbered lots in blocks 276 to 289, most of them vacant and the streets east of 3rd marked not open. A row of auto houses with concrete block walls, a garage and a few dwellings stand near Railroad Avenue and Broadway. Along the west edge the West Jersey and Seashore (P.R.R.) tracks run north and south between Broadway and New Broadway, with a pedestrian tunnel at Town Center; a Methodist Episcopal church with a fire station and Public School No. 2 stand on New Broadway. Below Browning Lane lies the curving street plan of the wartime village: Bergen, Haakon Road, Hannevig Avenue, Maud Avenue and Wilson lead to the circle of Noreg Place, with Christiana, Nansen Avenue and Horten Avenue around it and Mount Ephraim Road along the south-east side. These blocks are built up with frame dwellings and brick row houses, and fire alarm rings stand in Noreg Place and at Hannevig Avenue. Brooklawn Public School, drawn from plans, stands south of Browning Lane, and a club house on Browning Lane. Large blocks to the east and south (299, 313, 321, 327 to 329) are empty. The letters of Brooklawn are spread across the development.
notes: Modern names: Centre is Center Street, Bergen is Bergen Street, Christiana is Christiana Street, Maud Avenue is Maude Avenue, Horten Avenue is Horton Avenue, Hannevig Avenue is North and South Hannevig Avenue, Broadway is Old Broadway.
4th, 5th, 6th and 7th Streets are marked not open.

Gloucester City series sheet 22, Center Township, Jan 1923, 100 ft to an inch. Eastern Noreg village: New Broadway, Railroad Av, Centre and 2nd-6th Sts (not open), Browning Lane, Noreg Pl circle, Haakon Rd, Bergen, Hannevig, Horten, Maud, Nansen, Christiana, Mt. Ephraim Rd. One part.
